title.narrative: 2.2: To set up actions enhancing discussion and awareness of the human rights dimensions of trade and investment policy

description.narrative: An online communications platform was designed and launched; receiving over 2,900 unique visitors from 105 countries in 2020 alone. One hundred and seven (107) communications products were produced, including regional and countryspecific products. These included videos, social media campaigns and news articles. These products focused on furthering public discourse and greater appreciation of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human rights, and its impact on human and womens rights (Output 2.1). Communications activities were prioritized during the reporting period due to the COVID19 pandemic. While other project activities suffered the consequences of movement control orders, limited availability of stakeholders and a shrinking programming space, online communication activities gained momentum. Communications products were developed and shared with the public to raise awareness of thematic areas of business and human rights; and further shared on the curated web platform. Additionally, the promotion of events and the dissemination of knowledgebased products were supported through communication activities. Communication efforts in the reporting period also highlighted EUUNDP partnership on furthering the business and human rights agenda. Communication products published in 2020 include: videos, social media posts, online articles, news releases, webpages, newsletters, print brochures, rollups, event flyers.

title.narrative: 3.1: Access to remedies for parties subject to adverse human rights impacts is strengthened through awareness raising and rights provision

description.narrative: BHR Asia continues to strengthen the work done on access to remedies, with a particular focus on engagement of affected communities, as well as raising awareness on contextspecific concerns. In 2020, the project began work with civil society organizations in India, Sri Lanka and Thailand to better understand the concerns at the grassroots and subnational levels.In India, the CSO focused their work on women workers and indigenous peoples rights, with a view of conducting a baseline assessment of their access to remedy. In Sri Lanka, the CSO partner conducted research on business, human rights and the environment aimed at increasing awareness of this subject, and in Thailand ongoing work continues on research into access to remedy for Human Rights Defenders and training on AntiStrategic Litigation Against Public Participation.

title.narrative: 1: To support the regional momentum to strengthen Human Rights and environment protection in the context of business operations

description.narrative: BHR Asia provides curated support at national and subnational level to advance policy dialogue and partnership strategies in: India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka and Thailand. In late 2020, the project was launched in Mongolia.In 2020, this support resulted in the following outcomes:In Indonesia, UNDP supported inputs into the revision of the Omnibus Bill in the form of a policy analysisIn Myanmar, a consultation session on the Myanmar Land Law provided a series of recommendations for a potential Land Law reform. Additionally, as a direct consequence of the discussions initiated on the session the Union Federation of Myanmar Chambers of Commerce and Industries formed a UMFCCI Coordination Group on Land Use Matters.

title.narrative: 1.1: To set up actions enhancing common understanding and policy convergence with implementation of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights

description.narrative: In 2020, over 1,700 stakeholders were reached through online and offline events focusing on various BHRrelated topics aimed at enhancing a common understanding of the UN Guiding Principles (UNGPs) on Business and Human Rights. Participants included representatives from government agencies, business, academia, civil society, and international organizations. Training events were mostly focused on UNGPs and Human Rights Due Diligence. Group events and technical meetings organized allowed participants to discuss best practices on BHR and provide their inputs as part of the of NAP development process and implementation. Furthermore, participants had an opportunity to provide feedback on other related policies, such as Land Law in Myanmar.
